definitions.definition: Torus=reals/(2*pi*integers), with normalized measure dx/(2*pi). Periodic spatial products, integrals and derivatives are on this torus. A trigonometric polynomial is a finite sum of exp(i*k*x) with integer k.

For a periodic integrable f, hat f(k)=(2*pi)^(-1) integral_0^(2*pi) f(x)exp(-i*k*x) dx, k in Z. Extend Fourier coefficients to periodic distributions. Reality means hat f(-k)=conjugate(hat f(k)); mean zero means hat f(0)=0. For sequences, ell^2 is the square-summable sequence space with counting measure.

definitions.type: family of real or complex Hilbert spaces indexed by real order
definitions.definition: Write <k>=(1+k^2)^(1/2). H^s is the completion of trigonometric polynomials with ||f||_(H^s)^2=sum_{k in Z}<k>^(2s)|hat f(k)|^2, interpreted as distributions for s<0. L^2=H^0 and ||.||_2 denotes its normalized norm. For mean-zero f, ||f||_(dot H^s)^2=sum_{k!=0}|k|^(2s)|hat f(k)|^2. For s>=0, ||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s); for s<0, 2^(s/2)||f||_(dot H^s)<=||f||_(H^s)<=||f||_(dot H^s). In time L^infty norms are essential suprema, replaced by ordinary suprema for continuous representatives; derivative norms remain essential suprema.

definitions.type: one-parameter family of linear Fourier operators
definitions.definition: For real t, S_t=exp(-t*partial_x^3) has Fourier multiplier exp(i*t*k^3).
P0 f=hat f(0), identified with a constant function.
P=identity-P0, where identity is the identity linear operator.
Dinv=partial_x^(-1) has multiplier (i*k)^(-1) for k!=0 and zero at zero. Write Dinv2=(Dinv)^2=partial_x^(-2). Spatial differentiation partial_x has multiplier i*k.

definitions.type: family of time-step maps and finite trajectories
definitions.definition: For tau>0 and mean-zero f in L^2, define Ftau(f)=(1/6)P[(S_tau Dinv f)^2]-(1/6)S_tau P[(Dinv f)^2]. Define Htau(f)=(1/3)P[(S_tau Dinv f)*Dinv Ftau(f)]+(tau/9)(S_tau Dinv f)*P0(f^2)-(1/54)[S_(tau-s) Dinv[(S_s Dinv f)^3]]_(s=0)^(s=tau)-(1/(27*tau))[S_(tau-s) Dinv2[(S_(s-tau) Dinv2 Ftau(f))*(S_s Dinv f)]]_(s=0)^(s=tau). Brackets are upper endpoint minus lower endpoint and products are spatial products. Psi_tau(f)=S_tau f+Ftau(f)+Htau(f). For a positive integer L, tau=T/L and t_n=n*tau; U^0=u0, U^(n+1)=Psi_tau(U^n), 0<=n<L. This is the unmodified scheme with no frequency cutoff. Its elementary L^2 well-definedness and continuity are proved below.

definitions.type: averaged covariance of two real phases
definitions.definition: For tau>0, M_tau g=tau^(-1) integral_0^tau g(s)ds and eta_tau(alpha,beta)=M_tau(exp(-i*s*(alpha+beta)))-M_tau(exp(-i*s*alpha))*M_tau(exp(-i*s*beta)).
For integers a,b,c and k=a+b+c, set p=a+b, alpha=3*a*b*p, beta=3*k*c*p, Phi=alpha+beta=k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3.

definitions.type: family of trilinear Fourier operators initially on mean-zero trigonometric polynomials
definitions.definition: For tau>0, real base time t_n and k!=0, hat R2_(t_n,tau)(f1,f2,f3)(k)=-(tau/(18*i*k))*sum_{a+b+c=k,a+b!=0}exp(-i*t_n*Phi)*eta_tau(alpha,beta)*hat f1(a)*hat f2(b)*hat f3(c), with zero coefficient at k=0; Phase gives alpha,beta,Phi. Write R2^n_tau for t_n=n*tau. Bounded extensions, when used, are proved below.
B_t(f,g)=S_(-t) partial_x[(S_t f)(S_t g)]. Initially use smooth inputs; the negative Sobolev extension to L^2 inputs is proved below.

For I=[a,b], C_I(f,g,h)=integral_a^b S_(-t)P{P[(S_t f(t))(S_t g(t))]*(S_t Dinv h(t))}dt. Constant inputs are identified with constant time paths. At smooth inputs this is an ordinary integral, and the source estimates supply its continuous extensions.

definitions.type: family of bilinear integrated quadratic stages
definitions.definition: For a base time a>=0, step tau>0, t in [a,a+tau], and constant mean-zero inputs f,g, F_a(t;f,g)=(1/2)integral_a^t B_s(f,g)ds. Abbreviate F_a(t;f)=F_a(t;f,f). Its endpoint representation and extensions are proved below.

definitions.type: stepwise interpolation and residual construction from a smooth trajectory
definitions.definition: For tau>0, t_n=n*tau, and a finite smooth mean-zero trajectory f_n, on I_n=[t_n,t_(n+1)] put F_n(t)=F_(t_n)(t;f_n,f_n), z_n=f_n+F_n, C_n(t)=integral_(t_n)^t B_s(f_n,F_n(s))ds, Q_n(t)=(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(F_n(s),F_n(s))ds, W_n=Q_n(t_(n+1))+R2_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n), V(t)=f_n+F_n(t)+C_n(t)+Q_n(t)-((t-t_n)/tau)*W_n, and Y_n=V-z_n. Put rho_n(t)=-integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,z_n)ds-(1/2)integral_(t_n)^t B_s(Y_n,Y_n)ds-((t-t_n)/tau)*W_n. The residual path mathcalR is the concatenation of these increments: mathcalR(0)=0 and mathcalR(t)=sum_(j<n)rho_j(t_(j+1))+rho_n(t) on I_n. This construction does not assert endpoint compatibility; that is proved when f_n are the twisted Scheme trajectory.

inputs.statement: There is an absolute C>0 such that the following bounds hold uniformly in time. For mean-zero f,g in L^2 and all real t, ||Dinv f||_(H^1)+||Dinv f||_infinity<=C||f||_2, ||B_t(f,g)||_(H^(-pstar))<=C||f||_2||g||_2, ||J_t(f,g)||_(H^1)<=C||f||_2||g||_2, and ||Dinv P(fg)||_2<=C||f||_2||g||_2. For mean-zero A, ||A||_(H^(-pstar))<=||Dinv A||_2 whenever the latter is finite; ||J_t(A,g)||_2<=C||Dinv A||_2||g||_2. For all A,A2 in H^1, the algebra bound is: ||A*A2||_(H^1)<=C||A||_(H^1)||A2||_(H^1). S_t is unitary in every H^s, preserves reality/mean and is strongly continuous. For continuous, piecewise time-smooth spatially smooth mean-zero paths f,g on [a,b], integral_a^b B_t(f,g)dt=(1/3)[J_t(f,g)]_a^b-(1/3)integral_a^b[J_t(f',g)+J_t(f,g')]dt. Also J_t is symmetric and integral_I J_t(B_t(f,g),h)dt=C_I(f,g,h). In particular F_a(t;f,g)=[J_s(f,g)]_(s=a)^(s=t)/6 for constant inputs. All bounded product maps extend from polynomials by density.

For smooth mean-zero f, tau>0 and grid base t_n=n*tau>=0, let F_n(t)=F_(t_n)(t;f,f) and A_n(f)=integral_(t_n)^(t_n+tau) B_s(f,F_n(s))ds. The twisted update corresponding exactly to Scheme satisfies v^(n+1)=f+F_n(t_n+tau)+A_n(f)-R2_(t_n,tau)(f,f,f) when f=v^n=S_(-t_n)U^n. The source remainder's zero coefficient is zero and its nonzero coefficient is -(tau/(18*i*k))*sum_{a+b+c=k,a+b!=0}exp(-i*t_n*(k^3-a^3-b^3-c^3))*eta_tau(3*a*b*(a+b),3*k*c*(a+b))*hat f(a)*hat f(b)*hat f(c). This is an algebraic identity and has no numerical convergence premise.
source_conditions: tau>0, t_n=n*tau>=0, and f is a smooth mean-zero periodic input.
The update is the exact source scheme (1.4), with no cutoff, transformed by v^n=S_(-t_n)U^n.

output.statement: For each fixed tau>0, Psi_tau from Scheme is a continuous polynomial map from mean-zero L^2 to mean-zero L^2, preserving reality; Ftau maps L^2 continuously to H^1. Smooth data produce smooth iterates. For any trajectory produced by Scheme from smooth mean-zero data, f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n, the Interp construction has V(t_n)=f_n, V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1), is continuous and piecewise smooth in time and spatially smooth, and has mean-zero values, which are real whenever the initial datum is real. On each open step, V'=B_t(V,V)/2+mathcalR', where mathcalR'=-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. Thus mathcalR is continuous with the defining increments and the displayed residual identity holds a.e.

argument.text: For fixed tau>0, N006 gives Dinv:L^2->H^1 and the H^1 algebra bound. Thus Ftau is a continuous quadratic L^2->H^1 map. The first Htau term is a product of two inverse derivatives followed by P. The second uses the continuous bilinear mean P0(f^2), bounded by ||f||_2^2. The third has an H^1 cubic product followed by Dinv. The fourth has Dinv2 Ftau(f) and Dinv f, again an H^1 product followed by Dinv2; all coefficients, including tau^(-1), are finite for fixed tau. Hence Psi_tau is continuous from mean-zero L^2 to L^2. Every output is mean-zero: the first and third/fourth corrections have P or an inverse derivative; the mean of the second term is zero because Dinv f has zero mean. Conjugate Fourier symmetry and the real coefficients give reality. Smoothness is preserved by these operations, so finite smooth trajectories exist without any bound on their higher norms.

produces.statement: At each fixed positive tau the displayed Scheme is a continuous real mean-zero L^2 map and preserves smoothness.

argument.text: For any smooth input f at grid step n, identify source exp(t*partial_x^3) with S_(-t). The source Ftau,Htau formulas are exactly D008, term by term, with coefficients 1/6,1/3,tau/9,-1/54,-1/(27*tau), and identical endpoint signs. The source inverse derivative and mean have the same multipliers. In the twist, S_(-(t_n+tau))Ftau(S_(t_n)f)=F_(t_n)(t_n+tau;f,f), also following from N006's endpoint formula. The source cubic remainder has alpha=3ab(a+b), beta=3kc(a+b), the covariance eta and the prefactor -tau/(18ik), exactly R2. E005 therefore yields f_(n+1)=f_n+F_n(t_(n+1))+C_n(t_(n+1))-R2^n_tau(f_n,f_n,f_n). Substitution in Interp makes Q_n(t_(n+1)) cancel with its part of W_n; hence V(t_n)=f_n and V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1).

produces.statement: For every smooth mean-zero Scheme trajectory, V(t_n)=f_n and V(t_(n+1))=f_(n+1), where f_n=S_(-t_n)U^n. Its exact twisted update is f_(n+1)=f_n+F_n(t_(n+1))+C_n(t_(n+1))-R2_(t_n,tau)(f_n,f_n,f_n).

argument.text: Endpoint matching gives continuity across all grid points; all ingredients are spatially smooth and piecewise time-smooth. On a step F_n'=B_t(f_n,f_n)/2, C_n'=B_t(f_n,F_n), Q_n'=B_t(F_n,F_n)/2. Thus V'=B_t(z_n,z_n)/2-W_n/tau. Since V=z_n+Y_n, expansion gives V'=B_t(V,V)/2-B_t(Y_n,z_n)-B_t(Y_n,Y_n)/2-W_n/tau. The last three terms are precisely rho_n' and hence mathcalR' on that step. The concatenation is continuous at its endpoints and starts at zero. The mean and reality properties follow from F001 and the real, mean-zero operators used throughout. Quantify the smooth trajectory and fixed tau to obtain the asserted conclusion.
